findings: Facilitator PDF 30 printed 23 recommends at least four hours and three OSH learning outcomes. PDF 19 printed 12 image table confirms four hours.
Reference PDF 21 printed 13 introduces OSH, PDF 22 printed 14 lists sharps/infection/strain, PDF 23 printed 15 lists stress/accidents. Both image-only tables visually inspected.

Deck OSH spans actual slides 69–78, not inventory 74–83. Decision exercise is 70–71; five hazards are 73–75; 76–77 are demonstration/practice suggestions. Inventory reference printed pages 16–17 is inconsistent with actual 13–15. Original PDFs take precedence; source transcriptions remain unchanged.

TESDA unit 400311216 PDF 29–32 (printed 25–28) covers identify/prepare/perform and requires observable evidence. PDF 90 printed 86 allocates 1h + 1h + 2h. Four new lesson allocations total 4h but do not duplicate that original three-outcome hour distribution or establish certification equivalence.

Historical sharps disposal, PPE/disinfectant recommendations, benefit lists and exercise suggestions are not new authority for BHW procedures, mixtures, benefit eligibility or treatment. Only dummy/paper exercises are authored.

authoritative_web.checked: Infection risks and prevention via standard precautions/hand hygiene; no invented infection outcome or treatment protocol.
Reports exposure immediately; immediately seek medical care. Administrative/engineering controls preferred; PPE is one component. No US phone numbers or treatment regimens copied.
Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene; no specific procedure sequence introduced.

The basic competencies expected from the BHWs, and the recommended minimum 
hours of training, according to the TESDA Training Regulations on Barangay Health 
Services NCII, are the following:
BASIC COMPETENCIES
12

OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH
Recommendations on training
1.
This satisﬁes the “practice occupational safety and health policies and 
procedures” basic competency with at least 4 hours of training. 
2.
As per TESDA Training Regulations on BHS NCII, the following are the 
expected learning outcomes from this competency training: 
a.
Identify OSH compliance requirements
b.
Prepare OSH requirements for compliance
c.
Perform tasks in accordance with relevant OSH policies and procedures
3.
The trainer may discuss each of the hazards presented in the Manual, and may 
demonstrate how each is considered a health risk. 
4.
The BHWs may be asked to share their experiences on the hazards speciﬁed 
in the Manual. They may also be asked if they encountered other hazards in 
their performance of their tasks as BHWs.
5.
Demonstration may include the ways on how to avoid the workplace hazards. 
This may include doing the following: 
a.
Proper disposal of needles or syringes
b.
Brief demonstration of infection control practices
c.
Exercise to prevent back pain and other musculoskeletal pains

OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH
Bilang health workers ng komunidad, laging may posibilidad na magkaroon ng mga 
panganib sa paggawa ng kanilang mga tungkulin. Mahalagang matukoy ang mga 
panganib o hazards na ito, at maalis o makontrol ang mga ito sa lugar na 
pinagtatrabahuan at sa komunidad upang maisagawa ng ligtas ang mga gawain 
bilang BHW.

to appropriate personnel
